chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Buddy Rich's hands and why Catlett fit any band
summary: Crawford calls Rich the owner of the greatest hands but says Catlett had taste and could fit any band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I mean -- now, did you -- but how did you -- I mean like when you say something like what you liked about Webb was his speed, that that was most of what you liked about it --

Well, his drumming and his speed. He was a fast little drummer. Yeah, he played. And Buddy, naturally I like his speed, because that man practiced his single strokes. He's got great hands. He's got some of the greatest hands I ever saw.
Who do you think has the greatest hands that you've ever seen?

Buddy Rich. That's right. But when it came to taste and touch -- well, he had that also. Big Sid Catlett, people like that had that taste and touch and thought. I idolized Big Sid Catlett. And, well, Buddy Rich was -- he was in there also. That man was -- I don't know whether -- who he studied from, but he got himself straight and got himself right. Oh, he's a technician on those drums in his way.
When they'd put him in the pit, he wouldn't fit because he was too fast. Well, he wouldn't bein the pit no way. He wouldn't have been in there. That's below his dignity, I think.

But now -- let's see. Well, I was trying to get you to be a little bit more specific because it makes it sound, if you say, in other words, what I mean is like, if you say -- if I said, what do you like about Sid Catlett, you say --
-- his -- no, in other words, what I'm saying is, if you say his speed, his hands and the way he thought --
Then if I asked you about Chick Webb, and you say, his speed, his hands and the way he thought, well, it makes it sound, I mean --

Well, Chick wasn't in that category to me when it came -- he was a great drummer, but Big Sid was like out there on his own; with his speed and his thoughts, he'd fit any band. Chick Webb wouldn't because he was the boss of his band. Oh, yeah. There's a difference. It's hard to explain unless you, you know, you just consider yourself that the man was a great drummer. Big Sid could fit in any band, even in the pit. That's something else to say.
And he could read. I know he could read. But mostly he played head drums.
